# Station handbook

This fixture corpus belongs to an invented lighthouse station. It exists so
that nova-memory's verbs can be exercised — and shown failing — against a
corpus that ships with the tool and depends on nothing outside this
directory. Nothing here describes any real place, and no adopter should keep
it: build your own from your own record, and write your own gold set beside
it.

The station keeps three kinds of record, and the top-level directory is the
class. Root files like this one are the standing handbook. The `notes`
directory holds distilled working knowledge, one subject per file, each
carrying frontmatter. The `log` directory holds dated entries that are never
edited after the day they describe.

A distilled note earns its place by being the answer somebody needed twice.
An entry in the log is evidence that a thing happened; a note is the lesson
drawn from it. The two are not interchangeable, which is why retrieval hands
back the class of every hit: finding your sentence already written in a dated
log entry means the event was recorded, not that the lesson was ever banked.
